complaint: Netflix was buffering last night.

truth.why: Everything is normal right now. Last night isn't visible in this data, but nothing here is broken.

complaint: The speed test says 900 but it still feels slow.

truth.why: Gigabit fiber with low latency. Nothing in the network is slow.

complaint: Is my internet slow?

truth.why: A modest DSL-class plan working as designed: steady latency, no loss, no bloat.

complaint: I saw on X that Comcast is down. Is mine affected?

truth.why: Radar shows a Comcast outage somewhere, but this connection measures perfectly. Outages are regional.

complaint: Zoom freezes whenever my kid is gaming or downloading.

truth.why: Idle latency 14 ms jumps to 486 ms under download. Classic bufferbloat in the router or modem.

complaint: Video calls break up when I upload files to Google Drive.

truth.why: Upload saturation pushes latency to ~900 ms. Upload-side bufferbloat, common on cable.

complaint: Games lag only in the evening when everyone is home.

truth.why: Healthy at idle, 300+ ms once the line is busy. Busy household plus bufferbloat.

complaint: Websites take forever to start loading, then load fast.

truth.why: Lookups take ~1.8 s while speed and latency are perfect. The DNS resolver is the bottleneck.

complaint: Some sites just don't open. Others are fine.

truth.why: 2 of 5 fresh names fail to resolve; the line itself is clean. DNS problem.

complaint: Everything feels sluggish when I click a link.

truth.why: A slower but healthy plan with ~700 ms lookups. The click-to-load delay is DNS.

complaint: Everything is slow and Zoom keeps dropping.

truth.why: Every target is slow and lossy, and Radar reports an outage for this provider right now.

complaint: Nothing loads at all.

truth.why: Total loss of connectivity, confirmed by a Radar outage for the provider. (Radar is checked by our server, so it still loads.)

complaint: Slow on Wi-Fi, so I plugged in a cable. Still slow.

truth.why: Bad on Wi-Fi and equally bad on a cable. Wi-Fi is ruled out. It's the line or the provider, with modem/router a distant second.

complaint: Upstairs bedroom is unusable for calls.

truth.why: Bad upstairs, perfect next to the router, same device. Wi-Fi coverage.

complaint: My laptop is slow but my phone seems fine.

truth.why: Same room, same Wi-Fi, other device is fine. The laptop (driver, VPN, old Wi-Fi card) is the problem.

complaint: Wi-Fi drops constantly since we got a new microwave.

truth.why: Wired is perfect, Wi-Fi is lossy. 2.4 GHz interference inside the home.

complaint: Only Zoom is laggy. Everything else is fine.

truth.why: Zoom takes 312 ms while the Cloudflare edge takes 15 ms and Google 21 ms. The path to Zoom is the problem, not the home line.

complaint: Netflix buffers but YouTube is perfect.

truth.why: Only the Netflix server is slow to reach. A routing or peering issue between the provider and Netflix.

complaint: Netflix shows an error page.

truth.why: Netflix returns 503 while everything else is fast. Netflix is having a problem.

complaint: Can't join my Zoom meeting.

truth.why: Zoom times out while the rest of the internet is fine. Zoom-side failure, or the path to it.

complaint: Everything is slow tonight.

truth.why: Slow, jittery and lossy to every target, no Radar outage, no retest. Weak Wi-Fi and a sick line look identical from a browser.

complaint: Calls keep cutting out.

truth.why: Speed is fine but jitter and loss are high everywhere. Could be Wi-Fi interference or line noise.

complaint: The internet randomly freezes for a few seconds.

truth.why: Short freezes with loss but good speed. Wi-Fi roaming, router, or line, can't tell.

complaint: Downloads are really slow.

truth.why: Low download, everything else clean. Could be a weak Wi-Fi link rate, a cheap plan, or provider throttling.

complaint: Pages load slowly everywhere.

truth.why: High latency to every target including the nearby edge, low jitter, no loss. Bad routing at the provider, or a VPN/proxy on the device.

complaint: My video calls are choppy and my partner's are too.

truth.why: Two devices affected points away from one device, but both could be on the same bad Wi-Fi.

complaint: Everything is slow and I think Comcast is down.

truth.why: User blames Comcast, but Radar shows no outage. The data fits Wi-Fi just as well as the provider.

complaint: Slow in the evenings, fine in the morning.

truth.why: Evening slowdowns fit provider congestion, but a busy home Wi-Fi does the same. One snapshot can't tell.

complaint: The internet drops for a minute every few hours.

truth.why: A healthy snapshot can't rule out an intermittent drop. The honest answer is 'looks fine now, test when it happens'.

complaint: Zoom froze for everyone in my meeting earlier.

truth.why: Everyone froze, so it was likely Zoom, but it's over and this data can't confirm it. Any of these with honest hedging is fine.

complaint: My Zoom calls freeze for a few seconds at random.

truth.why: Real measurement: 10 ms idle, 741 ms while uploading. Severe upload bufferbloat; calls freeze whenever a backup or sync uploads.

complaint: My Zoom calls freeze for a few seconds at random. My phone at the same desk seems fine.

retest.where: phone at the same desk, same Wi-Fi

truth.why: Real measurement, with the phone retest (fast.com, 00:39 ET): same spot, same Wi-Fi, 310/180 Mbps and 26 ms loaded. The line and the router are fine; the laptop's Wi-Fi link is the bottleneck. A router fix (SQM) would be the wrong advice.

complaint: Netflix 4K stutters when someone else is downloading a game.

truth.why: Latency rises ~110 ms under download. Moderate bufferbloat, the most common home complaint.

complaint: Every new website takes a beat before it starts loading.

truth.why: A slow provider DNS resolver (~365 ms), nothing else wrong.

complaint: The basement office is slow, upstairs is fine.

retest.where: same laptop upstairs near the router

truth.why: Same laptop, good near the router and bad in the basement. Wi-Fi coverage.

complaint: Internet has been bad all evening.

truth.why: Degraded everywhere and Radar reports a provider outage right now.

complaint: My video calls freeze whenever my photo backup is running.

truth.why: Upload saturation pushes latency to ~440 ms. Upload bufferbloat.

complaint: We have satellite internet in the countryside. Video calls always lag.

truth.why: 600+ ms idle is the physics of a geostationary satellite, not Wi-Fi. The connection type is the cause; nothing at home fixes it.

complaint: Wi-Fi says connected but no new website will open.

truth.why: All 5 fresh names fail while already-known sites (cached) still answer fast. The DNS resolver is dead.

complaint: My online game keeps rubber-banding, but speed tests look great.

truth.why: Loss with perfect speed and latency. Wi-Fi interference or a noisy line; one test can't tell.

complaint: I can't upload anything. Photos and files just hang.

truth.why: Upload collapsed to 0.8 Mbps while download is full speed. Typical of a cable upstream fault, but a bad Wi-Fi link can also look one-sided. Bufferbloat is a symptom here, not the cause.

complaint: Hotel Wi-Fi says connected but nothing loads.

truth.why: Every site answers with a redirect (302). That's a login page (captive portal) on the local network, not an outage.

complaint: Only Google is slow. YouTube and Gmail crawl, other sites are fine.

truth.why: Google 291 ms vs edge 15 ms with everything else normal. Path to Google.

complaint: Netflix and Zoom both stopped working at the same time.

truth.why: Two unrelated services fail while Cloudflare and Google answer. More likely a provider routing problem than two outages, but this data can't prove it.

complaint: Our smart TV keeps buffering.

truth.why: The test ran on a phone and the line is healthy. The TV itself (its Wi-Fi or app) wasn't measured, so 'you're fine' with high confidence is wrong.

complaint: My home Verizon internet is slow.

truth.why: The user says Verizon, but the test ran over T-Mobile: the phone was on cellular, not home Wi-Fi. This test didn't measure the home connection at all. (Based on Mihir's real phone test.)

complaint: Sites are slow to start and video calls lag when the kids game.

truth.why: Two real problems at once: slow DNS and bufferbloat. Naming either one is right.
